item.title: Coinbase’s Ryan VanGrack Says Crypto Clarity Is Advancing
item.description: Coinbase Vice Chair Ryan VanGrack says legislation has stalled since the Clarity Act vote, but the SEC and CFTC are advancing regulatory measures that are providing another route to clarity. He added that crypto is inherently bipartisan, even as regulatory proposals may face congressional scrutiny and debate. He speaks with Romaine Bostick on "The Close." (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Bloomberg Businessweek Daily Podcast: Chip Stocks Rebound
item.description:
The people, companies and trends shaping the global economy. Watch Carol and Tim LIVE every day on YouTube: http://bit.ly/3vTiACF
A rebound in chipmakers propped up the stock market as dip buyers emerged despite economic data that reinforced speculation the Federal Reserve will boost rates in December. Technology stocks staged a sharp recovery, but whether that holds is another matter. Meantime, President Trump said he was tapping longtime aide Stephen Miller as his new chief of staff and that Susie Wiles will move to his political operation, shaking up his White House team days after a devastating midterm result. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Bremmer: U.S. Retreat From Global Leadership Is a Long-Term Shift
item.description: Ian Bremmer says Tuesday’s election should be viewed against structural changes in U.S. policy that are likely to persist regardless of which party holds the White House. He cites weaker support for free-trade agreements and a greater reliance on industrial policy, subsidies and tariffs. Bremmer speaks with Romaine Bostick on "The Close." (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Affordability First, Open to Hegseth Impeachment: Rep. Moore
item.description: Rep. Gwen Moore (D-WI) says affordability is “top of mind for all Americans” and believes health care is an obvious place for Democrats to intervene. Rep. Moore says Democrats' agenda should not be “first and foremost” to impeach people, but says she will not push for impeachment of Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth and that it would be “hard not to vote yes” on Rep. Thomas Massie's privileged resolution. She speaks with Kailey Leinz and Joe Mathieu on Bloomberg’s "Balance of Power." (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Rep. Beyer: Democrats Were Not Elected to Impeach Trump
item.description: Rep. Don Beyer (D-VA) says he was thrilled that a federal judge temporarily blocked President Donald Trump's planned triumphal arch from breaking ground. Rep. Beyer says he is depending on the courts and public sentiment to stop the project and has legislation aimed at preventing it from moving forward. Rep. Beyer says Democrats were not elected to impeach President Trump, but to stop the war and bring health care back to Americans. He speaks with Kailey Leinz and Joe Mathieu on Bloomberg’s "Balance of Power." (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Manchin: Democrats Risk Overplaying Hand on Impeachment
item.description: Joe Manchin, former US Senator and Governor for West Virginia, says Democrats can overplay their hand if they make impeaching President Donald Trump a priority after taking control of Congress. Manchin says Democrats should instead pass legislation addressing tariffs and public officials profiting from their positions and “try everything possible to put the genie back in the bottle.” Manchin says Trump will have to work with Congress because executive orders “only go so far and only last so long.” He speaks with Kailey Leinz and Joe Mathieu on Bloomberg’s "Balance of Power." (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Xi Taps Military ‘Hatchet Man’ to Rebuild China’s Army Command
item.description: As President Xi Jinping moves to rebuild a military leadership gutted by corruption purges, he’s betting that the man who oversaw the ousters can be trusted to replenish the ranks.
item.dc:creator: Bloomberg News

item.title: Markets Rebound After Historic Tech Selloff
item.description: The Close brings you the latest news and analysis leading up to the final minutes and seconds before and after the closing bell on Wall Street. Today's guests are AllianceBernstein Head of Equities Nelson Yu, Baird Strategas Managing Director of Policy Research Jeanette Lowe, FIGS CEO & Co-Founder Trina Spear, Sweetgreen CEO & Co-Founder Jonathan Neman, Elanco Animal Health CEO & President Jeff Simmons, GenTrust Head of NY Office, Senior Client Advisor Mimi Duff, Eurasia Group President & Founder Ian Bremmer, Evercore ISI Senior Managing Director of Equity, Derivatives & Quantitative Strategy Julian Emanuel, Coinbase Vice Chair Ryan VanGrack, Bain & Company Aaron Cheris Global Head of Retail Aaron Cheris, & Catch Hospitality Group Co-Founder & Partner Eugene Remm. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Paraguayan President Peña Removed From Office, Arrested
item.description: Paraguay’s Senate removed President Santiago Peña from office Friday, a dramatic downfall that paves the way for him to face potential criminal charges over his alleged role in the collapse of a major bank.
item.dc:creator: Ken Parks

item.title: US Sanctions Eight Canadian Companies Over Iran Transactions
item.description: The US imposed sanctions on eight Canadian entities over allegations that they enabled international transactions involving Iran.
item.dc:creator: Magdalena Del Valle and Yash Roy

item.title: Trump Names Miller Chief of Staff as Tech Rebounds
item.description: President Donald Trump said he was tapping longtime aide Stephen Miller as his new chief of staff and that Susie Wiles will move to his political operation, shaking up his White House team days after a devastating midterm result. We get analysis from Jeff Mason, Bloomberg Washington Correspondent & 'Balance of Power' co-host Kailey Leinz. Meantime, US stocks pared earlier gains as investors questioned whether the worst of a historic tech selloff is over and dissect the artificial intelligence trade. Bloomberg's Seth Fiegerman takes a closer look, while AIB Data Centers CFO Jolienne Halisky joins for our CFO Briefing. Plus - Grindr CEO George Arison discusses the company's latest earnings report. All on the latest edition of Bloomberg Businessweek Daily. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: 'Blue Wave' & Your Wallet, Managing Market Volatility
item.description: Bloomberg Money takes the pulse of your financial life, powered by the reporting of our global newsroom. Today's guests: Citi Wealth Chief Investment Officer Kate Moore and TIAA Financial Literacy Co-Author & Stanford Institute For Economic Policy & Research Annamaria Lusardi. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Houston Mayor Limits ICE Cooperation After Democratic Sweep
item.description: Houston Mayor John Whitmire ordered the city’s police to limit cooperation with US Immigration and Customs Enforcement, saying “elections matter” days after Democrats swept to power across Texas.
item.dc:creator: Joe Lovinger

item.title: DOJ National Security, Conspiracy Probe Leaders Step Down
item.description: The head of the Justice Department’s National Security Division and the US attorney handling a sweeping probe of President Donald Trump’s adversaries resigned Friday.
item.dc:creator: Ben Penn and Chris Strohm (Bloomberg News)

item.title: What Investors Need to Watch as Congress Returns: Debt Ceiling, Iran
item.description: The debt ceiling leads a packed agenda.
item.dc:creator: Nathan R Dean

item.title: Democrats Begin Outlining Priorities
item.description: On the early edition of Balance of Power, Bloomberg Washington Correspondents Joe Mathieu and Kailey Leinz discuss the dust settling on Tuesday's midterm elections. On today's show, Democratic Congressman Sam Liccardo of California, White House Council of Economic Advisers Chairman Chris Phelan, Stonecourt Capital Partner Rick Davis, Harvard Kennedy School Ash Center Visiting Democracy Fellow Jeanne Sheehan Zaino and former Republican Congressman Patrick McHenry. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Kansas 'More Purple' Than People Realize
item.description: Bloomberg's Brooke Sutherland joins Scarlet Fu and Tom Keene on "Bloomberg Money." They discuss the results of the US midterm elections. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: When Trump Cornered, He Lashes Back: Tim O'Brien
item.description: Bloomberg Opinion's senior executive editor Tim O'Brien joins Scarlet Fu and Tom Keene on "Bloomberg Money." They discuss affordability issues for Americans, and how President Trump may act after this week's 'blue wave'. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Europe Insists Russia Ends War Before Concerns Are Addressed
item.description: European nations want Russia to halt its war against Ukraine before entertaining any talk of the Kremlin’s concerns about the continent’s broader security architecture, people familiar with the matter said, a stance that risks putting them at odds with the US over the best way to end the conflict.
item.dc:creator: Alberto Nardelli and Alex Wickham

item.title: Canada to Give 200,000 Temporary Residents Permanent Status as One-Time Measure
item.description: Prime Minister Mark Carney’s government plans to transition up to 200,000 temporary residents to permanent residency by the end of 2027, in addition to its annual immigration target.
item.dc:creator: Nojoud Al Mallees
